newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australia bonds spring back,eye April high.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australia bonds spring back,eye April high.

text.p: *Australian bond futures surged higher in after hours trading, cutting through several resistance levels, and putting the market back on track towards last week's two-month highs.
*Market lifted by a strong rally in U.S. Treasuries after weaker than expected employment costs data.
Australian bond futures surged higher in after-hours trading, cutting through several resistance levels, and putting the market back on track towards last week's two-month highs.

The June 10-year bond futures contract ended SYCOM at 92.165, up smartly from Tuesday's 92.040 close, and continuing the bounce from just below the psychological 92.000 level seen at the beginning of the week.
The market was lifted by a strong rally in U.S. Treasuries after weaker-than-expected data for employment costs and goods orders.
The first quarter employment costs index rose 0.6 percent compared with a forecast 0.9 percent increase, while March durable goods orders fell 3.0 percent, its largest fall since last August.

The data helped to soothe fears of a tightening by the Federal Open Market Committee on May 20, but there are several more key indicators before then, and this week alone sees the first quarter GDP later on Wednesday and payrolls on Friday.
The U.S. 30-year long bond jumped over a full point in price and its yield dropped through 7.0 percent to end at 6.98 percent after 7.11 percent at Monday's New York close.

The local 10-year bond contract is expected to find some resistance at 92.180 before considering a renewed test of the 92.210/92.230 barrier, an area that the market failed to make a definite breach of last week.

Analysts feel as the SYCOM move was largely a reflection of the U.S. action, the local market could struggle to follow-through the move further ahead of its own key data on wages and retail trade later this week.
March balance of goods and services data is due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), and is forecast to rise A$150 million after the A$336 million increase in February.
